reasons: The two answers are nearly identical. Both correct the "real-name means adult recharge" premise at the start. Both write a letter that states the child is 11, gives 十余笔 and 6480 yuan, asks for a full refund, offers evidence and does not admit adult spending. Both cite 民法典 第十九条 and 第一百四十五条 plus the Supreme People's Court 意见（二）. Both give the right complaint path (customer service, WeChat order complaint, 12315, lawsuit) and the right payment fixes (免密, biometrics, password). Neither gives 法发〔2020〕17号 第9条, and neither says courts often reduce the refund for guardian negligence or reject claims with weak proof, so points 3 and 5 are equally thin, and both are far too long. The difference is in the extra specifics. B states an Apple "90 天内" window that Apple's own page does not give, which is the invented-deadline pattern the key warns about. B also has a WeChat bill-export path that does not match the real interface, and many unsourced menu paths. A stays vaguer on those points and attaches official links, which makes it a little safer. B's better Tencent platform naming and its 2021 notice link do not make up for that, so A wins slightly.
